question.leadin: This man fought Huascar (WAHS-car) during the War of the Two Brothers.
question.text: Name this ruler who was strangled at the hands of Spanish conquistadors after converting to Christianity. He lost his capital of Cuzco to the Spanish when he failed to fill a room with gold.
question.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
swap.text: This civilization, with capital at Cuzco and another city at Macchu Picchu, was conquered by Francisco Pizarro.
swap.clue: Descendants of this empire's royalty included Garcilaso de la Vega, and this empire was sometimes named for the four administrative suyus that it was divided into.

question.leadin: Answer the following about indigenous peoples of South America.
question.text: The Quechua group, who share their name with the language of the Inca Empire, live in and around this mountain range in Peru, Ecuador, and Bolivia.
question.clue: A culture in this mountain range depicted a spider called the "Decapitator" and created a mummy known as the Lord of Sipan.

swap.text: Diego de Ordaz is one conquistador who looked for the ceremonial place where this mythical chief covered himself in gold and jumped into a lake. The term is Spanish for "the golden one."
swap.clue: During the first part of the journey in which Orellana travelled the length of the Amazon, a valley of Cinnamon and this place were the targets of Gonzalo Pizzaro.

question.leadin: This country fought the Cenepa and Paquisha Wars against its northern neighbor, Ecuador.
question.text: Name this country, home to the cities of Arequipa and its capital, Lima.
question.clue: A president of this country was brought down after Channel N aired the first of the vladivideos, which showed a bribe being given to Alberto Kouri by national intelligence service chief Vladimiro Montesinos.

swap.leadin: The "trophy heads" collected by this culture featured a hole in the skull where a rope was threaded through.
swap.text: Name this culture who created geoglyphs in the shape of condors and hummingbirds in the desert, known as their namesake "lines."
swap.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

question.leadin: Answer some questions about European relations with the New World FTPE.
question.text: The Incas fought a disastrous battle with this Spanish conquistador at Cajamarca in 1532.
question.clue: Gonzalo also led a revolt against Blasco Nunez Vela for attempting to enforce the New Laws under Charles V. Another man with this surname served under Balboa and briefly served as mayor of Panama City.

swap.text: This city was the capital of the Inca Empire. Pachacuti remodeled this city and expanded its holdings to form the Inca Empire.
swap.clue: A chief of this puma-shaped city adopted a name roughly translated as "world turner."

question.leadin: The artist Cecilia Vicuna often hangs artworks named for these objects from ceilings.
question.text: Name these objects that were used for record-keeping and other purposes by the Inca.
question.clue: This devices that were made of string and were commonly used for keeping census records or for monitoring taxes. The information on these devices was stored using knots.

swap.leadin: Jim Woodmann constructed a balloon using primitive materials in order to show the plausibility of the "balloon theory" regarding these things.
swap.text: Identify these archaeological features which include the Condor and the Hummingbird. Jainer Jesus Flores Vigo was arrested for using a truck as an "attack against cultural heritage" on these things in 2018.
swap.answerHtml: Nazca Lines [or Nasca Lines; or Andes Lines; or Nazca Drawings]
swap.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

question.leadin: Early colonial writer Juan Freyle wrote an account of a ceremony in which a new ruler of these people was covered in gold dust and submerged in Lake Guatavita.
question.text: Name this confederation of Northern Andean tribes that was led by co-rulers called Zipa and Zaque. They were encountered by the Conquistador Gonzalo Jimenez de Quesada after his expedition sailed up the Magdalena.
question.clue: This people, who mined salt in large gacha pots and imported gold for tunjo figures of humans or animals at Guatavita.

swap.leadin: One hypothesis suggests that this culture may have created early hot air balloons to view certain artistic features.
swap.text: Name this Peruvian culture that succeeded the Paracas culture. These people carved stone geoglyphs, such as monkeys and spiders, into the desert in their namesake "lines."
swap.clue: Paul Kosok and Maria Reiche (RAI-keh) mapped structures created by these people.

question.text: Vilcabamba was founded by this Incan monarch. This monarch was captured by Spanish forces and imprisoned by the brothers of Francisco Pizarro before escaping and laying siege to Cusco for 10 months.

swap.text: Kidnapped Chinese workers were also kept in slave-like conditions on these Peruvian islands in order to harvest guano. Spain seized these islands in 1864, which prompted a war in which Chile and Peru fought to take them back.
swap.clue: Peruvian magnates on these islands hired blackbirders to kidnap workers to mine guano. Spain seized these islands to acquire those mines in the 1860s, but was repulsed by a coalition of South American countries.

question.text: The original "Maritime Foundations" theory was developed after the excavation of this site at the mouth of the Supe River that likely provided fish to Caral from the nearby ocean. This place is the type site of the Norte Chico.

swap.leadin: These people invented one of the first medium distance communication systems with two resin-coated gourds connected by a 75m length of twine.
swap.text: Name these people who had their capital at Chan Chan and who made use of the Spondylus shellfish and produced notably black shiny pottery.
swap.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.

question.leadin: This cloud forest culture created mosaic friezes at Gran Pajaten ("pa-ha-TEN"), built cliff tombs at Revash, and produced the Laguna de Los Condores textiles.
question.text: Name this culture that built the walled city of Kuelap in Amazonas, Peru. This culture's people were ascribed white skin by Inca chroniclers, whose reports of their ferocity inspired their nickname of "warriors of the clouds."

swap.leadin: A Spanish proverb says that to be "worth a" this city is to be worth a fortune.
swap.text: Name this city in Bolivia that was the location of the Spanish colonial mint and the major supplier of silver for Spain during their colonial empire days. The mines here were mythically founded by Huayna Capac.
swap.clue: Workers in this city still give offerings to a goat-headed underworld deity called "The Uncle" or El Tio.

question.text: In 2020, Algeria secured the repatriation of a number of these objects in the Museum of Man which were taken as war trophies from FLN fighters. These objects are drilled with holes during trepanation.
question.clue: Both the Paracas and the Nazca intentionally deformed these objects. The Chinook, Choctaw, and some peasant communities near Toulouse changed the shape of these objects in children with boards.

swap.leadin: In the best-known version of the Inkarri myth, a man with this name will be resurrected to throw off European rule.
swap.text: Give this name of the last ruler of a state defeated by Viceroy Francisco de Toledo. A later rebel adopted this name during his fight against the Bourbon Reforms.
swap.answerHtml: Túpac Amaru [accept Topa Amaru; accept Thupaq Amaru; accept Amaro in place of “Amaru”; accept José Gabriel Túpac Amaru II; accept José Gabriel Condorcanqui Noguera; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: The legitimate son of Manco Capac, he was captured an executed for the death of Friar Diego Ortiz.
